01 / THE CHALLENGE

The challenge

Clinical documentation competes for the same time and attention as patient care. Before expanding the product, the workflow needed to be tested in real consultations, with clear measures of accuracy and speed.

02 / THE APPROACH

The approach

Designed an 11-week hospital pilot spanning 371 consecutive outpatient consultations. Tested AI-assisted note generation in clinical workflows with physician review and quality oversight. Analysed revision requests, then refined specialty terminology, documentation templates and EHR field mappings.

03 / WHAT CHANGED

What changed

The pilot reported 91% documentation accuracy against physician-reviewed notes and a 20% reduction in per-note documentation cycle time. It demonstrated technical feasibility and clinician acceptability; sustained institutional adoption and revenue were not established.

IN THE DETAILS

What the accuracy measure means

Clinical partners reviewed sample notes against physician-reviewed reference notes. The 91% figure describes agreement between generated documentation fields and the physician’s assessment of documented findings and clinical reasoning; it is not diagnostic accuracy or independent clinical certification.

IN THE DETAILS

Following the revision requests

Root-cause analysis traced 60% of documentation revision requests to template field mappings and specialty-specific terminology. Addressing those gaps helped improve the workflow. The 20% time reduction reflects physician-reported documentation time through the system.

THE TAKEAWAY

A useful AI workflow needs more than a convincing demo. It needs a feedback loop that connects real usage, quality and time saved.
